# Venue: NeurIPS 2026 Main Track

Chosen on 2026-11-25 (venue-repo, answer to story-repo#2). Full requirement list with sources: `venue/neurips-2026-library.md` (the world's venue library, retrieved 2026-11-14). Template: `ht-role venue neurips --template DIR` (files `neurips_2026.sty`, `neurips_2026.tex`, `checklist.tex`).

## Why NeurIPS
- The objective asks for ICML, ICLR or NeurIPS, the latest official template, and "the venue's checklist (e.g. NeurIPS paper checklist)". NeurIPS is the only one of the three with a mandatory checklist that is part of the PDF, so the objective's checklist requirement has one unambiguous form.
- Single column, 5.5 in text block, 9 content pages: more room for figures and tables than ICML's 8 two-column pages. ICLR has the same 9 pages but no checklist and an edition already under review.
- Caveat on "latest": NeurIPS 2026 is the newest edition with a published call (the 2027 pages return 404 on 2026-11-14); its deadlines have passed, which does not matter for a template/standard. ICML 2027 / ICLR 2027 are newer editions; the objective allows any of the three, so this is a choice, not a gap. Re-check for NeurIPS 2027 only if the world's date passes its call.

## What binds the paper (all from the NeurIPS 2026 instructions and handbook)
- **Pages**: 9 content pages, figures and tables included. References, appendices, the checklist (and acknowledgments, which are hidden in anonymous mode) do not count and have no limit. Over-length is not reviewed. Camera-ready would be 10 pages (not needed here: a version is judged as a submission).
- **Layout**: US Letter, one column, text 5.5 in x 9 in, left margin 1.5 in; Times 10 pt on 11 pt; never edit the style file, margins or font sizes, never load `fullpage`/`geometry`/`savetrees`. Only Type 1 / embedded TrueType fonts (no Type 3 — matters for matplotlib: set `pdf.fonttype 42`).
- **Smallest type**: `\footnotesize` is 8 pt, `\scriptsize` 7 pt, `\tiny` 6 pt (style floors). The venue states no figure-font rule except "neat, clean and legible"; the paper's own standard is therefore: text inside figures at the size it prints, **not below 7 pt**, and preferably 8 pt or larger.
- **Float widths**: single-column page, so a full-width figure is `\linewidth` = 5.5 in; two side-by-side panels are about 2.7 in each; do not hand-position with absolute widths (give widths as multiples of `\linewidth`). Captions below figures, table title above tables, both lower-case except first word and proper nouns; the caption should state what is shown and a key take-away. Tables: `booktabs`, no vertical rules, centered. Figures should stay legible in black and white as well as colour.
- **Anonymous mode** (default, no `final`/`preprint`): no author names, no acknowledgments, own work in third person, links to code must be anonymous (an anonymised ZIP up to 100 MB is the safe form). The anonymous build prints line numbers and a "Submitted to NeurIPS 2026" footer; do not reference the line numbers.
- **Checklist**: mandatory, 16 items from `template/checklist.tex` (answers `\answerYes/\answerNo/\answerNA` plus a 1–2 sentence justification, questions unmodified, instruction block deleted but heading "NeurIPS Paper Checklist" kept). Placed after references and appendix; no page limit. A paper without it is desk-rejected. Item 16 asks for a declaration of LLM use; the handbook asks the description of LLM use in the experimental setup only when it is "important, original, or non-standard" in the approach. Here the studied LLM is the object of the experiment and is described in the setup anyway.
- **One PDF** (max 50 MB): content, references, appendices, checklist. Separate appendix PDF is not allowed. Code and data: a separate anonymised ZIP up to 100 MB (training/evaluation code, dependency specification, ideally self-contained and executable). Reviewers need not read the appendix or the ZIP, so everything a claim needs is in the 9 pages.

"""Fig 1 left panel: the search -> report -> verify protocol. Needs no data.
Coordinates are inches on the panel (2.7 x 2.3 in), so 7 pt text is checked by eye at print size.
usage: python figures/src/fig1_schematic.py OUT.pdf"""
import sys
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch, Rectangle
sys.path.insert(0, __file__.rsplit("/", 1)[0])
import figstyle as fs

W, H = fs.VENUE["panel_width_in"], fs.VENUE["max_height_in"]


def draw(ax):
    ax.set_xlim(0, W); ax.set_ylim(0, H); ax.axis("off")
    c = fs.C
    ax.text(0.02, H - 0.08, "Item pool, 5 folds", fontsize=8, va="center", weight="bold")
    fw = (W - 0.04) / 5
    for i in range(5):
        v = i == 4
        ax.add_patch(Rectangle((0.02 + i * fw, H - 0.40), fw - 0.03, 0.2, fc=c["fresh"] if v else c["light"], ec=c["ink"], lw=0.5))
    ax.text(0.02 + 4.5 * fw - 0.015, H - 0.30, "fresh", color="white", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7)
    ax.plot([0.02, 0.02 + 4 * fw - 0.03], [H - 0.45] * 2, color=c["reported"], lw=2)
    ax.plot([0.02 + 4 * fw, W - 0.01], [H - 0.45] * 2, color=c["fresh"], lw=2)
    ax.text(0.02, H - 0.55, r"$S$: $n$ items from folds 1–4", fontsize=7, color=c["reported"], va="center")
    ax.text(W - 0.01, H - 0.55, "held out", fontsize=7, color=c["fresh"], va="center", ha="right")

    bh = 0.52
    def box(top, title, lines, col):
        ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((0.04, top - bh), W - 0.08, bh, boxstyle="round,pad=0,rounding_size=0.05", fc="white", ec=col, lw=1.1))
        ax.text(0.10, top - 0.11, title, fontsize=8, weight="bold", color=col, va="center")
        for j, t in enumerate(lines):
            ax.text(0.10, top - 0.26 - 0.115 * j, t, fontsize=7, va="center")

    tops = [H - 0.72, H - 1.36, H - 2.0 + 0.0]
    tops = [1.58, 1.00, 0.52 + 0.0]
    tops = [1.60, 1.02, 0.44 + 0.0]
    tops = [1.58, 1.05, 0.52 - 0.0]
    tops = [1.58, 1.00, 0.42 + 0.0]
    tops = [1.58, 1.0, 0.42 + 0.0][:0] or [1.58, 1.02, 0.46]
    box(tops[0], "1  Search", [r"score $K$ configurations on $S$;", r"pick $\hat c$ = best on $S$"], c["ink"])
    box(tops[1], "2  Report", [r"best score on $S$ (the items that", r"chose it): $\hat\theta_{\hat c}(S)$"], c["reported"])
    box(tops[2], "3  Verify", [r"same $\hat c$ on fresh items;", r"gap = report $-$ fresh"], c["fresh"])
    for t in tops[:2]:
        ax.annotate("", xy=(W / 2, t - bh - 0.04), xytext=(W / 2, t - bh + 0.0), arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=c["ink"], lw=0.8, mutation_scale=7))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    fs.apply()
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(W, H))
    ax = fig.add_axes([0, 0, 1, 1])
    draw(ax)
    fig.savefig(sys.argv[1], bbox_inches=None, pad_inches=0)
EOF

shown.message:
The Fig 1 protocol schematic is redone to the venue's sizes. No data figures or tables exist yet, because experiment-repo hasn't delivered any result files.

- **Venue constraints:** venue-repo and paper-repo have answered. The venue is NeurIPS 2026, with a 5.5 in text width, figure text of at least 7 pt and full-width figures at most 2.3 in high. Tables are `booktabs` fragments.
- **Repo layout:** it now follows paper-repo's `.forgejo/CODEOWNERS`. Figures go under `figures/`, scripts under `figures/src/`, and tables under `tables/`. `figures/README.md` maps each file to its claim, script and source data.
- **Schematic:** the Fig 1 left panel is redrawn in inch coordinates at 2.7 × 2.3 in, with all text at 7 pt or larger. I checked the rendered image by eye. The PDF's fonts are embedded TrueType.
- **Pushed:** everything is on `main` of `figtab-repo`. I have not pushed to paper-repo's `dev` yet. The schematic is only half of Fig 1, so I'm holding it until the data panel can be composed with it.

Next, once experiment-repo's C1 gap-vs-n file and matrix-facts file arrive, I'll build Fig 1 and Tab 1. Fig 2–5 and Tab 2 follow as their data arrive. `experiment-repo`#3 (result-file format) is still open.
